title: Halmos counterexample: _claimRewards underflow on canonical 100e18 stake with growing accumulator
property: Anchor amount0 = 100e18 (CODE-002 canonical witness). Vary acc0, accDelta>0, withdrawnBps in (0, 10000). The next _claimRewards must not underflow.

counterexample.amount0_pretty: 100 phUSD (18 dec) — canonical CODE-002 stake size
counterexample.acc0_pretty: ~9.67e24 (achievable under standard 1e18-scaled accumulator after substantial reward funding)

trajectory: 1. user stakes 100e18 phUSD; at some checkpoint debt0 = 100e18 * acc0 / 1e18 ≈ 9.67e26
2. pauser pauses; user calls pauseWithdraw(81.92e18) — amount drops to 18.08e18, debt unchanged
3. accumulator grows by accDelta (reward funding cycle); acc1 = 2*acc0
5. _claimRewards computes (18.08e18 * acc1) / 1e18 ≈ 3.5e26 — far below debt0 ≈ 9.67e26 — Panic 0x11
interpretation: Confirms CODE-002 attack vector with a concrete, replayable witness on a realistic stake size (100 phUSD). The same calculation underlies `pendingPhUSD` and `pendingStable` view helpers (CODE-007).

crossReference.CODE-002: Directly verifies the steps listed under attackVector. The counterexample is a parametric refinement of the worked sequence.
